title: Global Tailings Portal as disclosure-denominator rail for tailings storage facilities
summary: The Global Tailings Portal is encoded as denominator-visibility infrastructure: it aggregates company disclosures about tailings facilities and gives communities, investors, regulators, and media a public information surface, while remaining dynamic and disclosure-limited.

status_history.note: Added as rev0026 impoundment/tailings correction rail.

subjects.name: GRID-Arendal / Investor Mining & Tailings Safety Initiative

claims.claim: The Global Tailings Portal says it brings together mining-company disclosures about tailings storage facilities and provides communities, investors, regulators, and media access to mine-waste information.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: At retrieval, the portal’s displayed dynamic counts included 222 mining companies, 297 mining operators, 692 mine sites, and 1,805 tailings storage facilities.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

claims.claim: This cube treats the portal as a disclosure rail rather than a complete global inventory or safety-verdict system, because the source language is about disclosed information and access, not independent verification of all facilities.
what_would_change_status: A second-pass source review materially revises the extraction, narrows its scope, or adds a stronger primary source.

type_payload.signal_capture_model: company disclosures assembled into searchable public portal
type_payload.outputs: public tailings-facility disclosure surface, dynamic counts, facility metadata access
type_payload.limitations: Dynamic and disclosure-dependent; not a complete or independently verified global inventory by itself; counts must be snapshotted and rechecked.

handling_notes: Infrastructure records are correction rails, not guarantees of correction or safety.
Avoid implying that standards, portals, or case-study sites replace regulatory authority, engineering judgment, community consent, or emergency preparedness.

unknowns: No facility-level records from the portal have been imported.
No independent verification/completeness audit has been attached.
next_actions: Snapshot and archive the portal counts periodically.
Pair with studies that audit public tailings databases and with operator conformance disclosures.
